title: Adding Currency and a Virtual Shop to Your Game on iPad
summary: Add coins and a virtual shop to your hyperPad game on iPad: show and save a balance, let players earn coins, and sell upgrades that make them earn faster.
body_markdown:
Adding currency and a virtual shop to your game on iPad takes two connected systems. Players earn coins during play, then spend them in a shop on items that make them earn faster. In hyperPad you build both with Behaviors, no code required. Get one coin source and one shop item working before you add more.


This guide follows the[Adding Currency and a Virtual Shop to Your Game](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/adding-currency-and-a-virtual-shop-to-your-game) tutorial in the hyperPad documentation. Open it alongside this post to see screenshots of every Behavior.


## Plan your currency and shop


Write down how your currency and shop should work before you open the Behavior Editor. The documentation tutorial uses a simple tapping game:


Rule Example


Starting balance 1000 coins for a new player


Earning Tap the cookie to earn coins


Click Multiplier Costs 100 coins and adds 1 coin to every tap


Passive Income Costs 200 coins and adds 20 coins every second


Use soft currency that players earn inside the game. Make it clear to players that coins have no real-money value and aren't an App Store purchase.


## 1. Show the balance


Add a Label to the Global UI and set its text to` 0` . This Label holds the balance, and because it's in the Global UI, every Scene shares it. Add a second Label next to it that tells the player what the number is, like "Coins".


## 2. Save the balance


Select the balance Label and open its Behaviors.


1. Add a[Receive Message](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/receive-message) Behavior that listens for an event called` saveMoney` .
2. Connect it to[Get Label](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/get-label) and choose the balance Label.
3. Connect that to[Modify Save File](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/modify-save-file) . Set the modification to **Set Key** and the key type to **Existing** .
4. Tap **Select or Create Key** , enter` Money` , and press **+** .
5. Plug the **text** output of Get Label into Modify Save File.


Now the balance saves whenever any Behavior in the Scene sends the` saveMoney` event.


## 3. Load the balance when the Scene starts


On the same Label:


1. Add a[Frame Event](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/frame-event) set to **Scene Start** , and turn on **Trigger on Restart** .
2. Connect it to[Load from File](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/load-from-file) and select the` Money` key.
3. Set **Default Value** to the starting balance, such as` 1000` . New players get this amount because they have nothing saved yet.
4. Connect it to[Set Label](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/set-label) and plug in the loaded value, so the Label shows the saved balance.


## 4. Let players earn coins


Pick something for the player to tap or collect. In the documentation tutorial it's a cookie. In the cookie's Behaviors, add 1 to the balance Label each time the player touches it.


Then save the change with a[Broadcast Message](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/broadcast-message) that sends` saveMoney` . Do this every time the balance changes, whether coins are earned or spent.


Close the game and reopen it. The balance should be where you left it.


## 5. Build the shop screen


Create a new[Layer](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/layers) called **Shop** and design it however you like. Give the player a button that shows the Shop Layer and another that hides it.


Give each shop item a Label for its current value and a **BUY** Label. Save and load each item's value the same way as the balance, with its own key.


## 6. Make the Buy button work


On the **BUY** Label for Click Multiplier, start the chain with a touch:


1. Use Get Label to read the balance.
2. Add an[If](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/if) Behavior that checks whether the balance is less than the price, 100.
3. If it is, use an[Alert](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/alert) to tell the player they don't have enough coins.
4. If it isn't, add 1 to the Click Multiplier value.
5. Subtract 100 from the balance and save with Broadcast Message.


Repeat for Passive Income. Only the price, the value it adds to, and the key it saves to change.


## 7. Make the items do something


Bought items need an effect in gameplay.


- **Click Multiplier:** in the cookie's Behaviors, load the multiplier from the save file and add that amount to the balance on each tap instead of 1.
- **Passive Income:** add a Label for it and place it off-screen so players can't see it. In its Behaviors, use a 1-second[Timer](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/timer) that reads the Passive Income amount, adds it to the balance, and saves.


## Take it further


Prices in this example never change, so items get easy to buy once players earn enough. Try raising each price after a purchase. You can also add more items, more ways to earn coins, or shops in other Scenes that use the same balance.


## Build your first shop item


Open your Project and set up the balance Label with saving and loading. Then add one way to earn coins and one item in the shop. Buy the item, close the game, and reopen it. Once the balance and the item are still there, add the next one.
